stories.title: Italy Maintains Border Controls Amid Spain's Retaliation Over Ceuta Migrant Crisis
stories.summary: Italy has refused to lift its border controls despite Spain's demand to do so, following a significant influx of migrants into Ceuta from Morocco. In response, Spain announced it would impose border checks on travelers arriving from Italy. This escalation marks a rare diplomatic spat between the two EU nations amid ongoing concerns over migration management.

stories.title: Trump Plans Supreme Court Appeal After Court Halts White House Ballroom Construction
stories.summary: A federal appeals court has blocked President Trump's $400 million ballroom construction project at the White House, ruling that he cannot proceed without congressional approval. The court's decision affirms a lower court ruling and allows only below-ground construction to continue. Trump has announced his intention to appeal the ruling to the Supreme Court, calling it unjust.

stories.title: Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan Establish Mutual Defense Pact
stories.summary: Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan have signed a mutual defense agreement, stating that an armed attack on any one of the three nations will be considered an attack on all. The pact aims to reshape the security dynamics in the region, particularly in light of ongoing conflicts. The agreement was formalized during a meeting in Mecca, although it does not specify the obligations for military action in defense of one another.

stories.title: Teenager Commits Deadly Shooting at School After Killing Grandparents in Thailand
stories.summary: A 14-year-old boy in Thailand killed his grandparents before opening fire at Debsirin Nonthaburi School, resulting in at least eight deaths, including his own. The attack, which occurred just outside Bangkok, left more than 30 others injured. Authorities reported that the boy used a firearm belonging to his grandfather and fired a total of 26 rounds during the incident. The motive for the shooting remains unclear.

This ruling is part of ongoing legal actions against Meta regarding its impact on young users. The company plans to appeal the decision and has previously faced additional fines related to similar issues.

stories.summary: The Senate has passed a bipartisan bill imposing stricter sanctions on Russia and extending existing sanctions on Iran. The legislation, which received an overwhelming vote of 86-11, was championed by the late Senator Lindsey Graham, whose recent death expedited its passage. The bill aims to penalize countries that continue to purchase Russian oil and gas, aiming to reduce revenue for Russia amid ongoing conflicts.

stories.title: Ceuta Faces Migrant Crisis with Thousands Still Present After Surge

While many migrants have returned to Morocco, a significant number are still unaccounted for, prompting the establishment of a missing persons office to assist families searching for their loved ones.
